newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH BUDGET SECURE DESPITE PAYMENT DELAY-BELKA.
newsitem.headline: POLISH BUDGET SECURE DESPITE PAYMENT DELAY-BELKA.

text.p: Poland's budget will be realised as planned despite a delay in payments to some public sector entities at the end of last week, Finance Minister Marek Bekla said on Wednesday.
"We are not threatened by a budget crisis," PAP news agency quoted Belka as saying.
"On Tuesday and Wednesday payments were continued, they are primarily headed to places where solvency was threatened. By Friday, all back payments will be made," he said.
The ministry did not send paychecks to some public sector workers across Poland at the end of last week.
It had said that holes in financing the budget deficit had occured during June, a month which seasonally brings in lower levels of revenue into the budget.

The National Bank of Poland's chief Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz on Wednesday said problems with this year's budget were partly inate because its spending and revenue targets were too ambitious and the deficit, at 2.8 percent of the gross domestic product, too large.
After the first five months of 1997, Poland's budget gap reached 53.8 percent of the 12.22 billion zloty shortfall planned for the whole of year, the ministry said on Tuesday.
Budget revenues in the January-May period amounted to 35.3 percent of this year's plan while spending in the same period reached 37.1 percent
In the corresponding period of 1996 revenues reached 36.1 percent of last year's plan, spending 37.5 percent and the deficit amounted to 51.9 percent.
